item.title: Stablecoins Are Becoming Financial Infrastructure — Not Just Crypto Infrastructure
item.description: Stablecoins have moved from a crypto-trading convenience to real payment rails used for remittances, payroll, and treasury. Here's what changed — and what hasn't.

item.title: Ethereum vs. Solana: What Are Developers Actually Building On?
item.description: A practical look at where developers build on Ethereum versus Solana — decentralized finance, tokenization, consumer apps, and the tradeoffs that actually drive the decision.

item.title: Why Wall Street Keeps Launching Crypto Exchange-Traded Funds
item.description: Why asset managers keep launching crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs), what a crypto ETF actually gives up versus holding crypto directly, and what the trend signals about institutional adoption.

item.title: Crypto Wallets Are Getting Easier to Use. Is the Seed Phrase Era Ending?
item.description: How account abstraction, passkeys, and social recovery are replacing the seed phrase as the default crypto wallet onboarding experience — and what tradeoffs come with it.

item.title: What Is a Blockchain Node — and Why Does Decentralization Depend on Them?
item.description: A plain-English explainer on what a blockchain node is, how it differs from a validator or a miner, and why the number and distribution of nodes determines how decentralized a network really is.

item.title: Tokenization Is Growing Fast. Does Everything Really Need a Token?
item.description: A clear-eyed look at what tokenization actually adds versus a traditional database, when putting a real-world asset or process on-chain solves a genuine problem, and when it's a token for its own sake.

item.title: The Senate Votes on the CLARITY Act Tomorrow. It Should Pass.
item.description: The Senate holds a cloture vote on the CLARITY Act on September 15, 2026. ChainBrief.news makes the case for passage — the roadblocks, the key senators, and what prediction markets are pricing in.

item.title: Circle Built Its Own Blockchain. The Gas Token Is USDC.
item.description: Circle's Arc layer-1 blockchain launched on mainnet with USDC as its native gas token, a permissioned validator set including BlackRock and DTCC, and sub-second finality. Here's what it actually is and why the timing matters.

item.title: Five Utility Tokens, Put to the Test
item.description: A skeptical, test-based look at five utility tokens — Chainlink, Filecoin, Helium, Render, and Livepeer — asking whether each one actually needs a token, or just has one.

item.title: Voices to Know: The Web3 Growth Marketer Podcasting About the Part Nobody Livestreams
item.description: An introduction to Stefan Furcoi's Trust to Traction podcast, a Web3 growth-marketing show covering user trust, onboarding, and go-to-market strategy for wallets, exchanges, and protocols — part of ChainBrief's Voices to Know series.

item.title: The CLARITY Act Failed. The SEC and CFTC Say They'll Regulate Crypto Anyway.
item.description: After the CLARITY Act's cloture vote failed 49-50 in the Senate, SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Michael Selig both said their agencies will pursue crypto rulemaking under existing statutory authority regardless of legislation.

item.title: What Is a Cloture? And Is the CLARITY Act Dead, or Dead for Now?
item.description: A plain-English explainer on Senate cloture procedure, why the CLARITY Act's cloture vote needed 60 votes, what happens after a failed cloture vote, and whether the bill is actually dead or just stalled.

item.title: Aave, Morpho, and Uniswap Just Deployed on a Chain They Don't Control
item.description: DeFi protocols including Aave and Morpho deployed on Circle's permissioned Arc blockchain at mainnet launch. Here's why, and the tension it creates with DeFi's permissionless roots.

item.title: Crypto Spent $206 Million on This Fight. It Lost Anyway. What Happens to That Money Now?
item.description: The crypto industry spent roughly $206 million in the 2026 midterm cycle backing the CLARITY Act, more than any other corporate interest — and the bill still failed. Here's why the spending didn't convert, and what the industry's political operation does next.

item.title: The Two Senators Who Might Still Save the CLARITY Act
item.description: A profile of Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC), the negotiators behind the CLARITY Act's ethics compromise, and why their work may be the bill's best remaining path forward — despite Gallego voting against cloture himself.

item.title: Why 18 State Attorneys General — Republicans and Democrats Alike — Wanted CLARITY Dead
item.description: An explainer on the 18-state, bipartisan attorneys general coalition that opposed the CLARITY Act over federal preemption concerns — the disputed 'qualified transaction' definition, the $11.4 billion fraud figure they cited, and what the objection means going forward.
